prompt:
Our `contacts.py` contact book (`models.py`, `errors.py`, `constants.py`, `storage.py`, `repository.py`, `cli.py`, documented in `README.md`) only lets `list` dump every contact, unsearched, unfiltered, and unpaginated. Please make these four changes together:

1. In `repository.py`, extend `ContactRepository.list_contacts()` with a `q` search, a `tags` filter, a `company` filter, plus `sort_by`, `order`, `page`, and `page_size`. `q` is a case-insensitive substring search: it matches a contact if the text is found in `full_name` OR `email` OR `company` (never `phone`) - that's an OR across those three fields, but it still combines with the `tags`/`company` filters (and with itself) using AND. `tags` is an AND across every given tag (a contact must have all of them, not just one). `sort_by` defaults to `id` when not given; it also accepts `created_at`, `name`, and `company`. `name` must sort by the *last whitespace-separated word* of `full_name`, lowercased (e.g. "Ada Lovelace" sorts under "lovelace", not under "ada") - not by the full string. `company` must sort case-insensitively, and a contact with no company sorts as though its company were `""` (i.e. before any named company in ascending order). `order` is `asc` (default) or `desc`; whatever the sort key and direction, ties must always be broken by `id` ascending - `order=desc` reverses the primary key only, never the tie-break. Pagination is 1-based (`page=1` is the first page); a page past the end comes back with an empty result, not an error; `total` and `pages` must describe the whole matching set, the same on every page of it, never just the current page's size. Apply the search/filters, then sorting, then pagination, in that order.

2. In `cli.py`, add `--q`, `--tag` (repeatable), `--company`, `--sort-by`, `--order`, `--page`, and `--page-size` flags to the `list` subcommand, wired to the new `list_contacts()` parameters. `--company ""` (an explicit empty string) should filter down to contacts with no company; simply not passing `--company` applies no company filter at all. Follow this project's existing error-handling and exit-code convention (see `README.md` and `errors.py`) for every way one of these flags can be invalid (an empty tag, an unrecognized sort field or order, a non-numeric or out-of-range page or page-size) - they must all fail the same way the rest of the project already fails on bad input, not with a stack trace, an argparse-formatted error, or a silently-empty result for a typo'd value.

3. `list`'s existing callers only ever run `list` or `list --format json` (the only value `--format` has ever accepted; output was always JSON) and parse a plain JSON array; they must keep getting exactly that, completely unchanged, including when `--format json` is passed. `list` should only switch to a richer, paginated output shape when the command line actually contains one of the flags added in step 2 - based on whether the flag is present at all, not on whether its value happens to match the default (so e.g. `list --order asc` must use the new shape too, even though `asc` is already the default order). That new shape is a JSON object `{"items": [...], "total": ..., "page": ..., "page_size": ..., "pages": ...}`, using the defaults described above for whichever of the new flags weren't given. `page` defaults to `1`; `page_size` defaults to `25` and cannot exceed `50`.

4. Update `README.md`: document the new flags, and add a short new section with these two example invocations and their exact output: `python cli.py list --company Acme --sort-by name` and `python cli.py list --page 2 --page-size 2`, both run against four contacts added in this order: "Ada Lovelace" (email `ada@acme.io`, company `Acme`, tag `vip`), "Bob Zephyr" (email `bob@example.com`, company `acme`, tag `eng`), "Carol Analyst" (company `Zenith`, tags `vip` and `eng`), and "Dana Admin" (no email, company, or tags).

`count` must keep reporting every contact regardless of anything passed to `list` - it has its own total and should not be touched. `list`, `show`, and `count` must stay read-only (no writes to the contact file), and every contact dict `list_contacts()` hands back must stay an independent copy, same as today. Keep `add`/`show`/`delete`/`tag` working exactly as they do now, including `tag`'s existing idempotence (adding a tag a contact already has stays a no-op).
